description:
PROBLEM
The small_scale_factor fixture these tests receive is tests/fixtures/utility_fixtures.py:67 and returns 1.0 (SCALE_FACTORS in tests/fixtures/benchmark_fixtures.py is not loaded as a plugin and is not the source). tests/test_h2odb.py, test_clickbench.py, test_tpcdi.py and test_ssb.py call generate_data() at scale 1.0; for H2ODB that is int(10,000,000 * scale_factor) rows from a pure Python loop (benchbox/core/h2odb/generator.py _generate_trips_data). Each test only asserts the returned table names (TPCDI: 16 files) and that the files exist; none checks row counts, contents, time or memory.

EVIDENCE (what is measured, and where)
- Trunk run 39633248681 (coverage on, since moved to trunk-coverage.yml): H2ODB 525 s, ClickBench 452 s, SSB 163 s, TPCDI 109 s.
- PR runs without coverage, p95 from run 39538637499 (stored in tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json): 364, 119, 93 and 35 s, which is 611 s of 2,994 s of medium time.
- Local macOS arm64 generation time (not CI), scale 0.001 / 0.01 / 0.1 / 1.0: H2ODB 1.9 / 3.5 / 31 / about 310 (extrapolated, not run); ClickBench 1.8 / 3.1 / 13 / 114; SSB 0.13 / 0.9 / 7.4 / 79; TPCDI 2.3 / 3.5 / 6.0 / 38, and 5.6 s at 0.11.
- Executed-line comparison across benchbox/ using the coverage API on the generators directly (not on the tests under pytest): H2ODB and ClickBench execute the same lines at 0.001 and 0.1; SSB at 0.01 matches 0.1 exactly but 0.001 misses ssb/generator.py:425,427,437; TPCDI at 0.11 matches 1.0 except utils/scale_factor.py lines 8-9 versus 14-17 (name formatting), while 0.01 skips the parallel FactTrade path (facts.py 29-35 and 79-144), which needs num_trades > 100000.
- Minimum scales that work: SSB 0.0005, TPCDI 0.001, H2ODB and ClickBench 0.00001. The benchmark registry's declared minimum is 0.01 for these four.
- History: the 1.0 value dates from the initial release (comment 'adjusted to minimum supported'); v0.2.1 (0182c9556) raised the H2ODB base row count tenfold and the fixture was not revisited.
- Other coverage of the properties someone might rely on: determinism tests/unit/core/tpcdi/test_deterministic_generation.py and test_ssb_generator.py:362; base row counts test_scale_factor_harmonization.py and test_wave_b_generators.py:26-29; TPCDI chunking test_generator_dimensions_facts.py:73-118.

FIX (chosen by an adversarial read-only review; options compared there: per-test scale, lower shared fixture, move to slow tier, patch base row counts, share datasets)
1. In each of the four modules, make test_generate_data build its own instance at an explicit scale, following tests/test_amplab.py:27-28 (AMPLab(scale_factor=0.01, ...)): 0.01 for H2ODB, ClickBench and SSB; 0.11 for TPCDI so num_trades stays above 100000 and the parallel path runs. Name the scale in a module constant, not a bare literal.
2. Remove the timeout(600) marker from the H2ODB test and timeout(300) from the ClickBench and SSB tests so the default 60 s limit is a real guard.
3. Optionally assert the written row count equals int(base * scale_factor) (manifest or line count); this adds a check on the formula that the current tests lack.
4. Leave the shared small_scale_factor fixture and the class-level fixtures (used by the query tests) unchanged.
5. After merge, regenerate tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json from a recent PR CI medium run (it drives shard balancing in trunk.yml, trunk-coverage.yml and ci.yml and the 900 s selection estimate in scripts/coverage_test_selection.py), then let the next trunk-coverage run rebuild the coverage map.
Estimated saving about 595 s of serial PR medium time; this is an estimate from local ratios and is NOT measured on CI.

GUARDRAILS (a change that violates any of these is not acceptable)
G1. Change only the four test_generate_data tests and, for step 5, the one durations fixture. Do not edit generators, the shared fixture, SCALE_FACTORS, workflows, timeouts elsewhere, or other tests.
G2. Do not lower a scale below the values above (SSB must stay at or above 0.01; TPCDI at or above 0.11). Do not pick a scale from timings alone.
G3. Do not weaken assertions. Every assertion in the four tests today (return type, expected tables, TPCDI's 16 files, file existence) must remain; the optional row-count assertion may only add.
G4. Do not mock, patch or stub the generator, the filesystem or random in these tests, and do not patch base_* row counts: the test must still run the real generate_data() path through int(base * scale_factor).
G5. Do not mark the tests slow, skip or xfail them, or raise any timeout to make them pass. Removing the larger timeout markers is the point; the default limit must pass.
G6. TPCDI's parallel FactTrade path must stay covered by a PR-tier (medium or faster) test. If it is not, add one explicit full-size test on the slow tier with real assertions in the same change, not later.
G7. Do not claim a time saving from local numbers. Report CI numbers from named runs, state which are local, and say what is unverified.
G8. Do not hand-edit medium_shard_durations.json; regenerate it with _project/scripts/update_test_durations.py --min-seconds 0.25 from named CI junit reports and record the run id in its source field.
G9. Standard repo rules apply: worktree, named fix/ branch, explicit staging, make comment-policy-check (no explanatory comments; the TPCDI scale rationale goes in the constant's name), self-review with the code review action before make pr-open, no attribution trailers.

OPEN QUESTIONS (not resolved by the review)
- Whether the benchmark constructors enforce the registry's 0.01 minimum anywhere callers reach (benchmark_registry.py:396 not traced).
- Whether benchmark_fixtures.small_scale_factor and SCALE_FACTORS are unused (not every reference traced); if unused, removal is a separate item.
- TPCDI memory at 1M trades (parallel path holds all chunks before writing, facts.py:97-110) is no longer checked per PR after this change.
